# @zakkster/lite-clock

Version: 1.4.1

Zero-GC simulation/timeline engine for @zakkster/lite-signal. SOA TypedArray
lane pool. Deterministic `advance(dt)` -- the only mutation entry point.
Single force-propagate frame signal carrying simTime; lane reads pull values
directly from TypedArrays so 10K lanes cost one signal write per tick.

Single-file ESM, ~1250 LOC, MIT, zero runtime deps, peer dep `lite-signal ^1.2.2`.

## Install

    npm install @zakkster/lite-clock @zakkster/lite-signal

## Imports

    import {
        createClock,
        LiteClockCapacityError,
        LiteClockReentrancyError,
        LiteClockDisposedError
    } from "@zakkster/lite-clock";

## Exports

### `createClock(config?)`

Factory. Returns a frozen `Clock` instance.

Config (all optional):
- `capacity: number` -- initial pool size. Default 1024, max 65534. Must be a
  positive integer.
- `growable: boolean` -- when true, the pool doubles on exhaustion up to
  65534; the final growth step clamps to the ceiling, so 65534 is reachable
  from any starting capacity. Must be exactly a boolean when present
  (`TypeError` otherwise -- `growable: 1` is a config error, never `false`).
  Default false (throws).

Validation is up front and fails closed: an unknown config key throws
`TypeError` with a did-you-mean hint ("createClock: unknown option 'capacty'
-- did you mean 'capacity'?"); shape errors throw `TypeError`, value errors
`RangeError`.

### `clock.advance(dt: number): void`

The ONLY mutation entry point. Validates `Number.isFinite(dt) && dt >= 0`
(throws `RangeError` otherwise). `dt=0` still increments `ticks` and
force-propagates the frame signal so subscribers observe the call.

Tick phases:
1. Validate dt
2. simTime += dt; tickCount++
3. In-place active-list compaction: iterate activeList, write positions back
   for survivors, queue completedIds for end-of-tick drain
4. `frameSig.set(simTime)` -- force-propagate (equals: () => false)
5. Drain onComplete queue (callbacks fire AFTER signal propagation)

Re-entrancy contract: the tick (compaction -> frame propagation -> onComplete
drain) is atomic. Calling `advance()` or `advanceTo()` AGAIN during the same
tick -- from an onComplete callback, an effect tracking `frame()`, or a
`frame.subscribe` subscriber -- throws `LiteClockReentrancyError`. All other
clock methods stay legal during the tick: `lane()` (with or without growth),
`dispose()`, `pause()`, `start()`, `reverse()`, `detach()`, `attachInterval()`.
Schedule follow-up advances for the next frame (queueMicrotask / rAF / your own
scheduler). Queued completions are never dropped: the drain runs in a finally,
so even a rethrowing effect fires the queue and leaves the clock usable.

### `clock.advanceTo(t: number): void`

Advance simTime to absolute `t`. Throws if `t < simTime`. `t === simTime` is
a no-op tick (dt=0 behavior). advanceTo is ABSOLUTE and UNSCALED: it reaches
`t` exactly at any `timeScale` (0 included -- an explicit destination overrides
the freeze). The 1.2.0 identity `advanceTo(t) === advance(t - simTime)` now
holds only at `timeScale === 1`.

### `clock.timeScale: number` (accessor)

Clock-wide rate multiplier, default 1. The getter never throws (read surface;
frozen value after dispose). The setter fails closed: on a disposed clock it
throws `LiteClockDisposedError`; a value that is not a finite number >= 0 throws
`RangeError` ("clock.timeScale: must be a finite non-negative number (got X)").
`0` is legal -- a true freeze in which `advance()` still ticks and propagates
the frame signal but completes nothing. `advance(dt)` scales the raw dt once at
entry (`dt * timeScale`); a finite product that overflows to non-finite throws
`RangeError` naming both `dt` and `timeScale`. Setting mid-tick is legal and
takes effect at the next `advance`. timeScale is replay state.

### `clock.lane(opts): Lane`

Allocate a new lane from the pool.

Opts:
- `duration: number` -- > 0, in sim-time units (typically ms)
- `onComplete?: () => void` -- fires once per completed cycle in the end-of-tick
  queue (loop/pingPong lanes fire it once per wrap)
- `loop?: boolean` -- when true the lane wraps at `duration` and never becomes
  DONE. Must be exactly a boolean when present (`TypeError` otherwise).
- `pingPong?: boolean` -- when true the lane wraps and flips reported direction
  every cycle (triangle wave). Must be exactly a boolean when present.

`loop` and `pingPong` are mutually exclusive: both true throws `TypeError`
("clock.lane: loop and pingPong are mutually exclusive"). Validation order:
shape -> unknown keys -> duration -> onComplete -> loop -> pingPong -> mutual
exclusion.

An unknown opts key throws `TypeError` with a did-you-mean hint
("clock.lane: unknown option 'onComplte' -- did you mean 'onComplete'?").

Throws `LiteClockCapacityError` if the pool is exhausted and `growable: false`.

### loop / pingPong lanes

A loop or pingPong lane is never DONE: `done()`/`donePeek()` report `false` for
its whole life, and `t()` cycles in `[0, 1)` (a `seek(duration)` edit parks it
at exactly 1 until the next advance). On any advance whose scaled dt
carries the lane past `duration`, the carry is recomputed from a stored base
(`startTimes = baseStartTimes + k*dur`, one rounding), so any dt partition
reaching the same total yields bit-identical positions/flags/cycleCounts.
`onComplete` fires once per completed cycle, including when a single dt spans
many cycles. There is no cap -- clamp pathological dts upstream; attachRAF/
attachInterval produce bounded dts. pingPong flips the same REVERSE flag that
`reverse()` toggles, so the two compose.

### `Lane` (handle)

Methods:
- `start()` -- begin advancing (or resume from a pause). Idempotent.
- `pause()` -- stop advancing; snapshots `positions[id] = elapsed`. Idempotent.
- `reverse()` -- toggle direction-of-reporting for position()/t(). Idempotent.
- `seek(p)` -- authored edit: clamp `p` to `[0, duration]` and jump there.
  Throws `RangeError` on a non-finite `p` (validation before clamp, on a live
  handle). seek NEVER starts a stopped lane (a DONE lane seeked below duration
  becomes PAUSED at `p`), NEVER fires onComplete, NEVER sets DONE, NEVER ticks
  the frame signal -- peeks see the new position immediately; tracked reads pull
  on the next tick. `seek(duration)` leaves position == duration WITHOUT
  completing: completion is advance-exclusive and needs a compaction pass, so a
  following `advance(0)` does NOT complete it while any `advance(dt > 0)` does.
- `restart()` -- seek to 0, then start. Re-bases an ACTIVE lane to 0 (stays
  active); clears DONE and runs a finished lane. Replaces the dispose/realloc
  replay pattern.
- `dispose()` -- free the slot back to the pool. Idempotent. Subsequent method
  calls on the handle are TRUE silent no-ops: the slot's generation is bumped on
  dispose, so a handle to a freed-and-reused slot proves stale (generation
  mismatch) and never drives or observes the new tenant.

Reads (tracked -- register dependency on the clock's frame signal):
- `position(): number` -- sim-time units, [0..duration]
- `t(): number` -- normalized [0..1]
- `done(): boolean`

Reads (untracked):
- `positionPeek(): number`
- `tPeek(): number`
- `donePeek(): boolean`

Stale handle: every method and read compares the slot's generation FIRST. A
stale handle (its slot was freed, maybe reused) returns inert terminals --
methods no-op, `position()`/`t()` return `0`, `done()` returns `false` -- WITHOUT
reading the frame signal, so a stale tracked read creates no reactive dependency.

Reverse mode: the engine advances `elapsed` forward always. `reverse()` flips
what `position()`/`t()`/peek variants return. Completion fires on forward
`elapsed >= duration` regardless of reverse flag -- a reversed lane "rewinds
to start" and completes at `t === 0`.

### `clock.frame: FrameAccessor`

`ReadSignal`-shaped accessor for simTime:
- `clock.frame(): number` -- tracked
- `clock.frame.peek(): number`
- `clock.frame.subscribe(fn): Dispose`

Force-propagates on every advance (even dt=0).

### `clock.attachRAF(): void`

Drive from `requestAnimationFrame`. Computes dt from the rAF timestamp and
calls the public `advance()`, so wall-clock dts ARE scaled by `timeScale` --
this is the intended slow-motion / fast-forward semantic. Throws if rAF is not
available (e.g. plain Node).

### `clock.attachInterval(ms: number): void`

Drive from `setInterval`. Computes dt from `performance.now()` between fires.
Node-side handles are `.unref()`'d so they don't block process exit.

### `clock.attachFixed(stepMs, opts?): void`

Fixed-timestep rAF driver -- the determinism keystone driver, replacing the
hand-rolled accumulator every deterministic consumer writes wrong once. Real
frame time accrues in an accumulator; the PUBLIC `advance(stepMs)` is called
a whole number of times per frame, so the sim only ever moves in exact
`stepMs` quanta (scaled once by `timeScale` like every advance -- the sim
quantum is `stepMs * timeScale`). The sub-quantum remainder ALWAYS carries.

`opts.maxSubSteps` (default 8) caps catch-up after a stall or tab suspend:
excess WHOLE quanta beyond the cap are DROPPED, never fed to the sim -- a
spiral-of-death guard that fails closed -- and counted exactly in
`stats().droppedMs` (real ms). Validation fails closed: disposed ->
`LiteClockDisposedError`; `stepMs` must be a finite number > 0
(`RangeError`); `opts` follows the config law (unknown key -> `TypeError`
with a did-you-mean hint; `maxSubSteps` must be an integer >= 1). Throws
where rAF is unavailable.

### `clock.detach(): void`

Cancel any attached tick source. Idempotent.

Each attach call replaces any prior attach.

### `clock.dispose(): void`

TERMINAL. Detaches any attached tick source, returns the frame signal's node to
the lite-signal pool, and retires every lane (each slot's generation is bumped,
so every outstanding handle proves stale). Idempotent.

Dispose is terminal, not a reset. `simTime` and `ticks` FREEZE at their last
values (they do not rewind). After dispose the mutation surface fails closed:
`advance`, `advanceTo`, `lane`, `attachRAF`, `attachInterval`, and
`frame.subscribe` throw `LiteClockDisposedError`. `frame()` and `frame.peek()`
return the frozen `simTime` (a number, never `undefined`). `detach()` and
`dispose()` stay idempotent no-ops. A `dispose()` from an effect/subscriber
firing during a tick is legal: the in-flight tick completes, then the next
mutation throws. Migration from a "reset and reuse" pattern: dispose means
dispose; create a new clock with `createClock()`.

**Required** for bounded-lifetime clocks (per route, per level, per
component mount) -- without it every `createClock()`/`dispose()` cycle leaks
one slot from the lite-signal default registry and the 1024th cycle hits
`CapacityError`.

### `clock.simTime: number` (read-only)
### `clock.ticks: number` (read-only)
### `clock.capacity: number` (read-only)
### `clock.activeCount: number` (read-only)

Plain getters. Not signals -- if you need reactivity, track `clock.frame()`.

### `clock.stats(out?): ClockStats`

Snapshot of pool + counter state. With `out` present it must be a non-null
object (else `TypeError`); it is filled and returned and allocates NOTHING (safe
in a hot loop). With `out` absent it allocates and returns a fresh object. Stays
readable after dispose (read surface; counters frozen). Fields, in order:
- `poolUsed: number` -- capacity - freeTop
- `poolFree: number` -- freeTop
- `peakActive: number` -- high-water active-lane count
- `totalTicks: number` -- tickCount
- `totalCompletions: number` -- completed cycles (callback-less lanes count too)
- `capacity: number`
- `timeScale: number`
- `droppedMs: number` -- real ms dropped by attachFixed's maxSubSteps cap
  (0 unless attachFixed has dropped; driver state, never in a snapshot)

### `clock.snapshotSize(): number`

Exact byte length of a snapshot at the CURRENT capacity:
`72 + 49 * capacity`. Pure read -- legal on a disposed clock. A growable
clock's growth changes it.

### `clock.snapshot(out: Uint8Array): number`

Capture ALL replay-observable sim state into the caller's buffer; returns
bytes written. Strictly ZERO-allocation -- per-frame rollback capture is the
design case: slab bytes are memcpy'd through cached internal views, and no
view is ever created over `out`, so `out` may sit at ANY byte offset (a
lite-rollback ring slot works as-is).

Scope: simTime, timeScale, tickCount, totalCompletions, peakActive,
activeCount, freeTop + the ten SOA slabs (startTimes, baseStartTimes,
durations, positions, flags, generations, activeList, activeIndex, freeList,
cycleCounts). NOT captured: onComplete functions (the live table is kept by
id -- see hydrate), attach/driver state (droppedMs included), the completion
queue (provably empty outside a tick).

Layout: versioned 72-byte header (magic, format version, capacity,
endianness canary) + 7 f64 scalars + packed slabs. NATIVE endianness with a
canary hydrate validates -- a snapshot is NOT a wire format (same-agent
restore only; no cross-machine contract).

Throws: mid-tick -> `LiteClockReentrancyError` (the atomic-tick law extends
to capture); non-Uint8Array -> `TypeError`; short buffer -> `RangeError`
(longer is legal). Readable on a disposed clock.

### `clock.hydrate(buf: Uint8Array): void`

Restore a snapshot onto THIS clock. Fail-closed guard ladder, in order, with
NO mutation until every guard passes: disposed -> `LiteClockDisposedError`;
mid-tick -> `LiteClockReentrancyError`; non-Uint8Array -> `TypeError`;
short header -> `RangeError`; bad magic / unsupported format /
endian-canary mismatch -> `TypeError` naming the field; capacity mismatch ->
`RangeError` naming both (same capacity REQUIRED -- growth mid-rollback is
not a thing); short buffer -> `RangeError`.

hydrate bumps NO generations: handles minted before a same-clock snapshot
stay valid after restore (that identity is the point). The live onComplete
table is preserved by id, so restore + re-advance REFIRES completions that
had fired in the rolled-back timeline -- onComplete side effects MUST be
rollback-aware or idempotent; that is the consumer's contract. Refire
fidelity is exact only across a rollback window containing no
`lane()`/`dispose()`: a slot disposed or re-tenanted inside the window has
lost or replaced its callback (the documented fidelity boundary). A handle
minted AFTER the capture addresses whatever the restore puts in its slot
(the ghost-handle hazard -- roll back state, not lane inventory). The
restore path allocates ~10 short-lived subarray views (minor-GC only);
capture is the zero-alloc side. Legal with a driver attached (the next
driver tick advances the restored state); legal onto a same-capacity virgin
clock (state transfers, handle objects do not).

THE ROUND-TRIP LAW: `snapshot -> hydrate -> advance(seq)` is BIT-IDENTICAL
to `advance(seq)` uninterrupted -- positions, flags, generations, free-list
order, carry state, counters, everything -- at any capture point,
loop/pingPong lanes included. Torture-gated across fuzzed capture points and
a 1000-run rollback drill.

### `LiteClockCapacityError`

Extends `Error`. Thrown by `clock.lane()` on pool exhaustion. Carries:
- `name: "LiteClockCapacityError"`
- `capacity: number` -- the pool size that was exhausted

Message names both escape hatches (`{ capacity: N }` and `{ growable: true }`).

### `LiteClockReentrancyError`

Extends `Error`. Thrown by `clock.advance()` / `clock.advanceTo()` when
re-entered during a tick (from an onComplete callback, an effect tracking
`frame()`, or a `frame.subscribe` subscriber). Carries:
- `name: "LiteClockReentrancyError"`

The tick is atomic; schedule follow-up advances for the next frame.

### `LiteClockDisposedError`

Extends `Error`. Thrown by the mutation surface of a disposed clock --
`advance()`, `advanceTo()`, `lane()`, `attachRAF()`, `attachInterval()`, and
`frame.subscribe()`. Carries:
- `name: "LiteClockDisposedError"`

The disposed check runs BEFORE the re-entrancy check, so a dead clock always
throws `LiteClockDisposedError`, never `LiteClockReentrancyError`. Reads
(`frame()`, `frame.peek()`, and stale handle reads) never throw and never return
`undefined`. dispose() is terminal; create a new clock.

## Key invariants

- `advance(dt)` is the only mutation entry point. dt validation is up-front;
  the hot loop has no per-iter validation.
- One force-propagate frame signal per clock. Lane reads pull from TypedArrays
  routed through clock getters (so growth-relocated arrays are transparent
  to live LaneHandle instances).
- In-place active-list compaction. Completed lanes drop out without a second
  pass.
- Frame signal propagates BEFORE onComplete callbacks fire. Effects tracking
  `lane.done()` see `true` BEFORE the callback runs.
- Atomic tick: re-entrant advance()/advanceTo() from an onComplete callback,
  effect, or subscriber throws LiteClockReentrancyError. lane/dispose/pause/
  start/reverse/detach/attachInterval stay legal during the tick; the drain
  runs in a finally so queued completions are never dropped.
- Pool is LIFO (free list is a stack). Most-recently-disposed slot is reused
  first. Each slot carries a `Uint32` generation tag, bumped on every disposal;
  a LaneHandle stamps the tag at `lane()` and compares first on every method and
  read, so a stale handle (freed, maybe reused slot) proves stale and takes the
  inert path -- it never drives or observes the next tenant.
- `clock.dispose()` is terminal and fails closed: the mutation surface throws
  `LiteClockDisposedError`; `simTime`/`ticks` freeze; reads return the frozen
  simTime (never `undefined`). detach()/dispose() stay idempotent no-ops.
- Reverse only affects reporting. Engine always advances elapsed forward.
- Pool exhaustion throws by default; `growable: true` doubles up to 65534
  (the final growth step clamps to the ceiling -- 65534 is reachable from any
  start). Config fails closed: unknown option keys on either door and a
  present non-boolean `growable` throw `TypeError` with a did-you-mean hint.
- `clock.dispose()` is required for bounded-lifetime clocks (releases the
  frame signal node back to the lite-signal pool).
- The atomic-tick law covers capture: `snapshot()`/`hydrate()` mid-tick throw
  `LiteClockReentrancyError`. Outside a tick the completion queue is provably
  empty -- which is why a snapshot need not carry it.
- The round-trip law: `snapshot -> hydrate -> advance(seq)` is bit-identical
  to uninterrupted `advance(seq)`. hydrate bumps no generations, requires
  equal capacity, and preserves the live onComplete table by id (refires are
  the consumer's contract).

## Common patterns

### DOM animation driven by a lane

    import { effect } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";
    import { createClock } from "@zakkster/lite-clock";

    const clock = createClock();
    clock.attachRAF();

    const lane = clock.lane({ duration: 300 });
    effect(() => { el.style.opacity = lane.t(); });
    lane.start();

### Chained transitions via onComplete

    const fade = clock.lane({
        duration: 200,
        onComplete: () => {
            const next = clock.lane({ duration: 300, onComplete: finish });
            next.start();
        }
    });
    fade.start();

### Deterministic test playback

    const clock = createClock();
    const lane = clock.lane({ duration: 100 });
    lane.start();
    [16.67, 33.33, 16.67, 8.33].forEach((dt) => clock.advance(dt));
    // simTime, position, done are 100% reproducible.

### Multi-clock for isolated subsystems

    const ui  = createClock(); ui.attachRAF();          // 60fps animations
    const sim = createClock(); sim.attachInterval(8);   // 125Hz physics

### Rollback capture/restore (lite-rollback-ready)

    const clock = createClock({ capacity: 1024 });
    const buf = new Uint8Array(clock.snapshotSize());   // preallocate once
    // per frame:
    clock.advance(16);
    clock.snapshot(buf);          // zero-alloc capture (~0.7 us at cap 1024)
    // on rollback:
    clock.hydrate(buf);           // restore; existing handles stay valid
    clock.advance(16);            // re-advance -- completions REFIRE

### Composition with lite-statechart

    const clock = createClock(); clock.attachRAF();
    let pulse;
    const machine = createStatechart({
        initial: "idle",
        states: {
            idle:    { entry: () => pulse?.dispose(), on: { START: "active" } },
            active:  {
                entry: () => {
                    pulse = clock.lane({
                        duration: 1000,
                        onComplete: () => machine.send("DONE")
                    });
                    pulse.start();
                },
                on: { STOP: "idle", DONE: "idle" }
            }
        }
    });

## What this is NOT

- Not a tween library (no easing curves -- compose with `lite-ease`)
- Not a state machine (compose with `lite-statechart`)
- Not async (no promises, no microtasks)
- Not a renderer (only computes lane positions)
- Not a scheduler with priorities (all lanes advance at the clock's rate)
- Not a wire format (snapshots are same-agent binary, canary-guarded;
  cross-peer sync is a future lite-room contract, not this one)

## Deterministic testing

`advance(dt)` is the sole mutation entry point. Inject any dt sequence twice
in two fresh clocks and you get identical state. `attachRAF` and
`attachInterval` are convenience wrappers that compute dt from real time and
call `advance()`; `attachFixed` is the deterministic driver (exact `stepMs`
quanta, fail-closed drop counter); tests should use `advance()` directly.
For capture/replay, `snapshot`/`hydrate` round-trip the full sim state
bit-exactly -- see the round-trip law above.

## Files

- `Clock.js` -- implementation (~1250 lines, ESM)
- `Clock.d.ts` -- TypeScript declarations
- `test/01..20` -- behavior, GC, dispose-leak, snapshot, fixed-step, and
  docs-drift regression suites
- `test/torture.mjs` -- the authoritative memory + determinism gate
  (`node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`; @zakkster/lite-leak +
  @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler; prints "ok" on success)
- `bench/bench.mjs` -- eight-scenario throughput + retention measurement
- `README.md` -- full architecture + integration recipes
- `CHANGELOG.md` -- versioned change log
- `ROADMAP.md` -- deferred features and rationale
